approach: Add one reading-acceptance check, `check_scope_limit` in crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs, as a single `step!(check_scope_limit(reading));` line in `refusing_check` after `check_defined_terms` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. Root cause: nothing at the reading gate compares a scope limit with the files Athena always writes (CHANGELOG.md, forced by `ensure_changelog`, reading.rs:297, run before the gate at reading.rs:859) or with the readers of a changed config. A limit written from the named files therefore passes the gate and fails at verification (class scope-criterion-too-narrow-misses-dependent-tests; jobs 20261018-045437-7z81 and 20261023-052543-9bw7). A scope limit is a criterion for which `athena_context::briefs::limits_changed_files` (briefs.rs:146) is true, the same matcher that builds the allowlist at verification (`allowed_paths`, briefs.rs:115). The check runs for capability `change` readings with no question and does two mechanical things, with no scan of repo contents. (1) CHANGELOG half, now structural (round 4, finding 4): find the limit's allowed-list span, the words from the first `only`/`outside`/`except`/`beyond`/`besides` up to the first change word after it. A limiting criterion is accepted when CHANGELOG.md is a word inside that span, or the exact phrase `the deliverables` occurs, or the criterion has none of those trigger words (a bare form such as 'No other file is changed' or 'production unchanged'). Otherwise it is refused. There is no negation word list: a name outside the span ('...; CHANGELOG.md is not changed') is simply not permitted, and a name inside it ('Only X and CHANGELOG.md may change, keeping one entry') is. (2) Config half: when a limit exists and athena.toml or defaults.toml is a deliverable, the reading needs a `Consumers:` assumption that (a) names one or more path-like words, none the config file itself, every one a deliverable (or under a deliverable ending in '/'), or (b) says 'unchanged' or 'no change', or (c) says 'none found'. This half also fires for the defaults-proposal job (`accept_request`, proposals.rs:442), whose reader will write 'No other file is changed': that job must carry a `Consumers:` line too, and the error text and the new READING_RULES line say exactly what to write. Support work: one READING_RULES line, unit tests in reading.rs, corpus cases with new input-form tags, a one-constant fixture fix in run/tests.rs (forced), a steward test showing stored proposals leave the queue, a replay step with a stop rule, a CHANGELOG entry and decision D166. The CHANGELOG entry and D166 map criterion 2's 'CHANGELOG.md listed' to 'named in the limit', with the evidence that `ensure_changelog` (reading.rs:859) already lists it at the gate, so a deliverable-only test could never fire.

decisions.choice: CHANGELOG half uses the structure of the limit sentence. For every criterion with `limits_changed_files` true, tokenize as the matcher does (lowercase, hyphen to space, trim non-alphanumeric ends). Trigger words: only, outside, except, beyond, besides. If none occurs, the criterion is bare and exempt. Otherwise the span runs from the first trigger word to the first change word (change, changes, changed, modified, touched) after it, or to the end. Exempt when the span holds the word `changelog.md` (the row from the default-written table), or the two-word phrase `the deliverables` occurs anywhere. Else refused. A CHANGELOG.md deliverable alone does not repair the text.
decisions.reason: `build_reading` calls `ensure_changelog` before `check_reading_acceptance`, so every change reading already lists CHANGELOG.md at the gate; a rule that accepted 'CHANGELOG.md listed' would never fire. The 9bw7 failure was a limit sentence that forbids the forced edit. The span reuses the shape `limits_changed_files` already parses ('only X may change', 'no file outside X changed'), so a name counts only where the sentence permits it. This answers round 4 finding 4: no free negation window ('keeping', 'kept', 'stays', 'remains' no longer matter), only the plural phrase 'the deliverables' exempts ('Only the deliverable src/a.rs may change' is refused), and 'than', 'apart' and 'aside' are dropped from the trigger list. Known misses, stated in D166: a limit with no trigger word that still forbids CHANGELOG.md, and a name placed in the span but negated inside it, are accepted; 'Only X may change; CHANGELOG.md may change too' is refused and repaired by moving the name into the list.

rejected.option: Accept when CHANGELOG.md is a deliverable (the literal reading of criterion 2)
rejected.why: Inert for every production reading, so the class stays open.

rejected.option: Free negation-word window around the name (rounds 2 and 3)
rejected.why: Finding 4: 'keeping', 'kept', 'stays' have positive uses and the window refused valid limits while missing other phrasings; the span needs no word list.

rejected.option: Exempt on any occurrence of 'deliverable'
rejected.why: 'Only the deliverable src/a.rs may change' omits CHANGELOG.md; only 'the deliverables' points to the list.

rejected.option: Fire only when the limit names a file (round 1)
rejected.why: Leaves 'test-only change' and 'only the docs may change' accepted although the job must still edit CHANGELOG.md.

rejected.option: Make `ensure_changelog` append CHANGELOG.md to a limiting criterion's text instead of refusing
rejected.why: It rewrites the reader's criterion silently, so the reader never learns that a limit must account for default-written files, and the config half would still need a refusal. The accepted reading chose refuse-and-repair before a producer runs.

decisions.choice: Only criteria are scanned; out_of_scope items are not. The matcher is `limits_changed_files` imported from athena_context::briefs; the tokenizer and span finder are small private helpers in checks.rs.
decisions.reason: One definition for the gate and for verification-time enforcement (`limiting_criterion` reads criteria only, briefs.rs:103-108), so the gate cannot drift from what is enforced. out_of_scope items are exclusions, never an allowlist, and 'files kept from job X' would cause false refusals. This departs from the reading's 'criterion or out_of_scope item'; raised as a User question.

rejected.option: A new phrase list ('only', 'nothing else', 'no other') as the trigger in checks.rs
rejected.why: A second matcher that would drift from `limits_changed_files`.

rejected.option: Also scan out_of_scope items
rejected.why: Enforcement ignores them, and exclusions would cause false refusals.

decisions.choice: The config half fires only with a limiting criterion (exempt from the CHANGELOG half or not, bare or not) and a deliverable whose normalized path is athena.toml or defaults.toml. It is met only by a `Consumers:` assumption (trimmed, case-insensitive prefix, like `code_surveys` in surveys.rs:116) in one of three forms: (a) at least one path-like word other than the config file, every path-like word a deliverable path or under a deliverable ending in '/'; (b) 'unchanged' or 'no change'; (c) 'none found'. Path-like = contains '/' or ends .rs/.toml/.md/.json/.yml/.yaml after trimming quotes, backticks, brackets, a leading './' and end punctuation. The refusal text states the repair: 'add an assumption `Consumers: <each file that loads <config>, listed as a deliverable>`, or `Consumers: none found` / `Consumers: <config> readers unchanged` if no file must change'.
decisions.reason: With a limit the deliverable list is the allowlist (briefs.rs:110-126). In 7z81 the tests that load the real athena.toml were not deliverables, so the scope guard failed the job; the introspection's prevention was that the reading should then allow those files. Requiring every named consumer to be a deliverable does that. athena.toml is also read outside crates/ (xtask/tests/policy.rs, xtask/src/main.rs), so every path-like word counts. Round 4 finding 3: the defaults-proposal job (`accept_request`, proposals.rs:442-450, sent through `ask` at proposals.rs:642 into `build_reading` and `check_reading_acceptance`) lists defaults.toml and tells the producer to touch no other file; its reader will write the bare criterion 'No other file is changed', which `limits_changed_files` matches, so the config half fires. Decision: it still fires. Applying a default changes what the tests that load the real defaults.toml see, which is the 7z81 failure; one `Consumers:` line is cheap and 'Consumers: none found' is accepted. The reading is refused at most once for this (the refusal text goes to the reader as the re-read feedback, reading.rs:688) because the text names the exact line; unit and corpus cases pin refuse without the line and accept with it. D166 records that proposal-apply jobs carry this line. This is a revised sense of criterion 3's 'either': a bare crates/ test deliverable no longer satisfies it, since that left 7z81's failure open.

rejected.option: Exempt bare limits on proposal-apply jobs from the config half
rejected.why: The 7z81 failure was a config change whose consumers were not allowed; a defaults change has the same risk, and an exemption keyed to the request text would be a hole in the rule.

rejected.option: Accept any crates/ test deliverable as the answer (the literal criterion 3)

rejected.option: Only check words containing crates/
rejected.why: An xtask/ consumer that is not a deliverable would pass, and one that is a deliverable would be refused.

rejected.option: Scan repo content for files that load the config
rejected.why: Out of scope; readers see a plain copy and the gate must stay deterministic.

rejected.option: Require the consumer rule for every config deliverable, even without a limit
rejected.why: Without a limit the producer may touch consumers freely; it would refuse readings that cannot suffer the failure.

decisions.choice: Default-written files go in a const table `DEFAULT_WRITTEN_FILES: [(&str, &str); 1]` whose only row is (`super::CHANGELOG_PATH`, reason text), and config files in `CONFIG_FILES: [&str; 2]`, both in checks.rs.

risks.risk: False refusals: `limits_changed_files` matches a criterion that mentions a limit in passing, and the CHANGELOG half refuses such limits unless the span names CHANGELOG.md.
risks.mitigation: The matcher already errs toward not matching (briefs.rs:140-145). The repair is one phrase ('and CHANGELOG.md' in the list, or 'the deliverables'), given in the error text. Bare forms stay accepted and are pinned by corpus Accept cases. Step 10 reads the replay and stops above 8%.

risks.risk: The Consumers rule cannot verify that the search was done; 'none found' can be written without searching.
risks.mitigation: D166 states the limit: the gate forces the question and checks that every named consumer is a deliverable; scanning repo content is out of scope. A consumer the reader does not name is the remaining gap and is named in D166.

risks.risk: The span rule refuses a valid limit or accepts a negated name.
risks.mitigation: The span rule has no word list for negation; the pinned forms are 'is not changed' and 'stays as it is' (Refuse, name outside the span), 'keeping one entry' and 'src not changed' (Accept, name inside the span). D166 names the remaining misses: a limit with no trigger word that forbids the file, and a negation inside the span. 'Only X may change; CHANGELOG.md may change too' is refused and repaired by moving the name into the list.

risks.risk: A defaults-proposal job fails reading twice and stalls (finding 3).
risks.mitigation: The refusal text names the exact line to add (`Consumers: none found` / `... unchanged` / listed deliverable paths), the new READING_RULES line says the same, and the refusal text is the re-read feedback (reading.rs:688). Unit and corpus cases pin refuse-then-accept for the accept_request shape. If a reader still fails twice, the job is refused through the unchanged ReadError::Refused path; the replay step 10 shows how often proposal-apply-shaped readings are refused.

risks.risk: The new READING_RULES line pushes a rule line past 220 bytes or the section past its bound.
risks.mitigation: Keep the line to about 200 bytes; if the section exceeds the bound, set the bound to the measured size plus a small margin and fix its comment. `cargo test -p athena-context` shows it. The reader prompt is untouched.

risks.risk: Another test or fake reader outside the places found pushes a limit phrase through the gate and starts failing.
risks.mitigation: Step 11 runs `cargo test --locked` for the whole workspace. A failing fixture gets 'and CHANGELOG.md' in its limit text, as LIMIT does; the check is not weakened.

risks.risk: run/tests.rs and steward.rs are not among the six listed deliverables, so a scope guard built from this job's deliverable list could flag them.
risks.mitigation: Both edits are small, listed in `files`, explained in the CHANGELOG entry and D166, raised as a User question and checked by `git diff --stat`. Exempting README.md-only limits in the check was rejected as a hole in the rule.

risks.risk: A Consumers line with a `./` prefix, quotes or backticks, or a prose word, is mis-parsed and refused.
risks.mitigation: Trim quotes, backticks, brackets, './' and end punctuation as `allowed_paths` does (briefs.rs:119-120); a deliverable ending in '/' covers paths under it; unit and corpus cases pin both forms. A word like 'e.g.' is not path-like (no '/', no listed extension).

risks.risk: The replay share exceeds 8% and holds the job.
risks.mitigation: Step 10 stops and reports the measured share; the producer does not narrow the check or edit the declared figure. The producer snapshot has no records/, so the replay may only be visible in the loop's output; if it is not visible, the producer says so in its output.

User: criterion 3 says a reading with an athena.toml deliverable and a limit passes by adding 'a crates/ test deliverable' or a `Consumers:` assumption. This plan passes it only when every consumer path named in the Consumers line is a deliverable, or the line says unchanged or none found; a bare test deliverable with no Consumers line stays refused, because that left 7z81's failure open. The same applies to the defaults-proposal job, whose reader must add `Consumers: none found` (or a real list). Say if you want the literal wording or a proposal-apply exemption instead.

User: the accepted reading says a scope limit may also be an out_of_scope item, and that listing CHANGELOG.md as a deliverable is enough. The code settles both: verification reads criteria only (briefs.rs:103-108), and the gate always sees the CHANGELOG.md deliverable because ensure_changelog runs first (reading.rs:859). This plan checks criteria only and requires the limit's allowed-list span to name CHANGELOG.md, or the text to say 'the deliverables', or to be bare. Criterion 2's 'with CHANGELOG.md listed' is shown as the limit naming it.
